applicant_utility.summary: With $4,000 as the ceiling and an 18-day window, this award rewards applicants who have already thought their project through. The selection panel is looking for three things: your track record on the issue, a clear account of how the initiative advances peace in New Zealand, and a timeline and budget that show the money will actually be spent. Unlike the Trust's education awards, entry is open to unincorporated groups, individuals enrolled at a tertiary institution, and formal organisations, so you do not need legal entity status to apply, but if a group applies the project leader must be a woman. Note that prior Trust recipients are excluded entirely, so this is a once-per-person opportunity within the Trust's portfolio.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A woman or female-led group with a concrete, near-ready peace-building project － mediation, conflict resolution, inter-community work, or eliminating family violence － that can be delivered with up to $4,000.
application_readiness_checklist: Draft the project outline, timeline and budget before 12 October, because the window is only 18 days
Write the budget against the three assessment criteria, making it obvious how the funds will be spent
Assemble evidence of your own experience organising or delivering similar work, since demonstrated capability is a stated criterion
Confirm no one on the leadership team has previously received a New Horizons for Women award
Locate the application confirmation email immediately after submitting, since the form or server may fault later and the Trust recommends keeping a copy
common_rejection_risks: Applying after 30 October 2026: the window is fixed and short, and no extension is published
Submitting a budget that does not add up to the initiative described, which directly fails the stated selection criterion
A group application whose project leader is not a woman, which is not eligible
Applying as a previous Trust award recipient, which the Trust excludes outright
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any part of the initiative that exceeds $4,000: for a community programme covering venues, facilitators or materials, this award is usually seed funding and the applicant should plan to raise or contribute the balance.
document_audit: The application confirmation emails occasionally land in a spam folder, so check there and save the confirmation
A timeline is explicitly required, so a narrative without dates is incomplete
alerts: The window opens on 12 October 2026, two days after this record was verified, so the form may not yet be live
Payment is normally in two instalments: 50% after signature of the acceptance document and 50% on completion, so budget for cash flow
Other Trust awards cannot be held simultaneously with this one
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online administration system linked from the Trust's Awards page: submit the project outline, timeline and budget inside the 12th-30th October window, and retain the browser confirmation and email copy.

applicant_utility.summary: At up to $10,000 for a single year of full-time STEM study, Toloa Tertiary is one of the larger Pacific-targeted awards in New Zealand, but the eligibility gates are narrow and unforgiving. You must be a New Zealand citizen or permanent resident of Pacific Islands descent, you must be in second year or beyond, and you must still be full-time － final-year and Year 3 students are excluded because the Government fees-free scheme is meant to cover them. Travel is explicitly not funded, and money for accommodation is limited to university hall residence, so students living at home or in private flats will not have rent met. Applications are handled through Le Va and the funds go to your institution, not to you, so keep your enrolment and invoice paperwork tight.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A New Zealand citizen or permanent resident of Pacific Islands descent in second or third year of full-time STEM study at a New Zealand tertiary institution who will not be covered by fees-free in their final year.
application_readiness_checklist: Gather documentary proof of Pacific Indigenous descent early: passport, birth certificate, or a grandparent's documents showing village and birthplace with linking surnames
Request a community leader endorsement letter on the institute's template if you cannot assemble family documents
Collect 2025 academic records, since these are required regardless of your grades
Get proof of full-time 2026 enrolment in a STEM-related programme at second-year level or above
List every scholarship or grant awarded or pending for 2026, including the First in Family scholarship; the page shows other Pacific awards you may already hold
Have your NSN ready, and expect a mismatch if you were born overseas and lack an NSN
common_rejection_risks: Being in final year or Year 3:these applicants are excluded because fees-free already applies, and this is an explicit rule
Submitting an incomplete application:only complete applications are reviewed
Failing to prove Pacific Islands descent through accepted documentation
Not being full-time, or falling below full-time enrolment during the study year
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs generally: accommodation is covered only for university hall residence, travel expenses are explicitly not funded, and award holders are advised the institutional scholarship should not exceed their individual scholarship entitlement before the award applies, so out-of-pocket costs remain substantial.
document_audit: Proof of descent must be documentary; a statement in the application form is not sufficient
